A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same automated SAE interpretation work. All 29 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original scoring comparisons, prompt and sampling ablations, SAE-versus-neuron evaluations, intervention experiments, and cross-layer alignment analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original scoring, ablation, and intervention results and adds human-rating validation, further scorer comparisons, and disagreement case studies.

M1.justification: V2 removes the auxiliary procedure that uses Hungarian assignment to align SAE decoder directions and then compares aligned interpretation embeddings (v1 Section 5). The main interpretation pipeline and all five scoring procedures remain substantively unchanged; expanded descriptions and terminology substitutions do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use RPJv2 and the uncopyrighted Pile for interpreting Gemma 2 9b and Llama 3.1 8b SAEs, retaining context-based and intervention evaluation. Human ratings and additional scorer comparisons validate the existing interpretation task. The removed cross-layer study analyzes the same SAEs rather than introducing or removing a separate data domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: V2 Table A9 adds Claude Sonnet 3.5 to the scorer-model comparison; v1 Table A7 evaluated Claude as an explainer. The corresponding explainer comparison, v2 Table A8, drops the randomly initialized TopK SAE comparator, although that baseline remains in other comparisons. Human-generated interpretations were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The correlation-study sample increases from 600 to 800 latents. V2 introduces a four-level human-rating protocol covering 700 contexts and 81 interpretations, with at least five contexts per interpretation, plus a 100-latent Claude simulation comparison. It also adds simulation evaluation to the explainer/scorer tables and a cost comparison standardized to 100 contexts. Existing prompt-ablation and intervention settings largely persist.

E4.justification: V2 adds four concrete score-disagreement case studies in Appendix A.4.7, human-rating validation, and expanded scorer sensitivity analyses. It removes the semantic-overlap and decoder-alignment studies from v1 Section 5 and Appendix A.6. The dataset, context-length, sampling, chain-of-thought, and SAE-size ablations are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use Spearman/Pearson correlations and report medians with interquartile ranges across latents, including the same layerwise variability plot. V2 extends these reporting practices to additional results but introduces no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or specified significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds human-score correlations of 0.69, 0.60, and 0.59 for fuzzing, simulation, and detection, respectively, along with cost estimates and simulation results in Tables A8–A9. Fuzzing–simulation Spearman correlation changes from 0.70 on 600 latents in v1 Table 1 to 0.75 on 800 latents in v2 Table A1; this is not a same-setting performance gain. Cross-layer overlap results disappear, while most retained ablation values and intervention plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Removing v1 Section 5 also removes its explicit permutation-symmetry argument and mathematical formulation of alignment through Frobenius inner products. The intervention-score and intervention-strength definitions in Equations 1–2 are unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws cross-layer semantic similarity as a claimed contribution and removes the conclusion recommending wider SAEs on fewer residual-stream layers. Its abstract also stops highlighting SAE-versus-neuron superiority, although that finding remains in the results. The central claims about scalable interpretation and five scoring methods are retained.

C2.justification: V2 develops specific explanations for disagreements between token localization, contextual relevance, and embedding-based scores, supporting a recommendation to combine scoring methods. V1 discussed these differences more generally. V2 also expands the cost-related limitations of interpreting long-range latents and removes the training recommendations derived from the deleted cross-layer study.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents the default 40-example interpretation prompt, names Stella-400M, specifies scorer roles, and discloses additional study sizes and token-cost accounting. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. The printed download target changes from auto_interp_explanations to auto_interp_interpretations, and Llama Neuronpedia links become specific to residual-stream and MLP resources; their availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the Hernandez et al. citation with Singh et al. in related work and changes attribution of quantile-based prompting from Bills et al. to Bricken et al. It removes alignment-related references to Ainsworth, Crouse, and Moschella, and drops the Lieberum/Gemma Scope citation. The broader positioning within automated interpretability remains similar.

P1.justification: V2 extensively replaces explanation/feature terminology with interpretation/latent, rewrites the methods around a three-stage pipeline, reorganizes interpretation generation, and expands the scoring narrative. It removes Sections 1.1 and 5, incorporates the separate SAE comparison subsection into Section 4.2, and restructures the appendix. These are substantial narrative changes beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adds a pipeline diagram as Figure 1, moves the original Figure 1 to Appendix Figure A1, and removes both alignment figures. It adds the cost table, relocates the main correlation table, and separates the explainer/scorer comparison into tables with additional simulation columns. Figure 3 changes terminology and corrects the random-explanation curve color without changing its plotted results.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the central scoring evaluation through human-rating correlations, explicit cost estimates, and concrete disagreement cases, while making the pipeline easier to follow. Removing the overlap study narrows the paper but also withdraws its associated training recommendations. The human validation remains small and lacks rater-agreement and uncertainty reporting, so the evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
